front.title: TCP Connectivity Probing Extension for Highly-Dynamic Networks

abstract.t: This document defines TCP OAM-ACK, a TCP extension for fast transport-layer connectivity detection in highly-dynamic networks such as LEO satellite constellations, high-speed rail, and ad-hoc intelligent agent networks. Traditional TCP keep-alive uses fixed long probe intervals and cannot rapidly differentiate genuine link outages from congestion-induced packet loss. TCP OAM-ACK negotiates capability via TCP SYN/SYN-ACK handshake using shared experimental TCP option [RFC6994]. A sender adaptively shortens probing interval upon consecutive probe ACK losses, triggers path-switching notifications to external path-control entities instead of mis-invoking TCP congestion window reduction. This mechanism acts like transport-layer BFD for TCP connections. This document describes option formats, sender/receiver behavior, fallback strategies, RTT-assisted early triggering, and interaction with path management modules.
